prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which designed small molecules recruit ubiquitin ligases to eliminate chosen proteins, through the PROTAC concept and the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type molecular glues

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1: targeted protein degradation (B023) with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The unifying chemical idea is induced proximity to the ubiquitin-proteasome system, realised by a designed small molecule that brings a chosen protein and an E3 ligase together. The chemistry is physical-organic in character, with ternary-complex cooperativity, linker design and ligand-binding thermodynamics, and the mechanism has been confirmed independently over two decades. Crews and Deshaies supply the concept and its first demonstrations. Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target is a separate mechanistic discovery that explains why the glue half of the field works and that is already supported by approved drugs (lenalidomide, pomalidomide). Together the three names cover both strands under one citation. I weigh the lack of an approved bifunctional degrader as a forward-looking risk, not as a defect in the discovery itself.
statement.case_against: Credit remains the weak point. Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure), Sakamoto (first PROTAC paper), Gray, Ito and Kim all have real claims, and a three-name cap omits at least one strand whichever way we cut it. The citation must be worded carefully so that it does not imply that PROTACs and molecular glues share a single history. The clinical payoff for bifunctional degraders is still unproven, and Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B002) is the cleaner, more mature and more settled attribution. If the committee concludes that the combined citation is misleading, I would prefer B002 over a narrowed B023 that I could not defend on credit.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers Ciulli to Handa in the third seat, because VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made PROTACs a general platform, and treats cereblon as target identification for one drug class.
responses.response: I have thought about this and I still prefer Handa, but I accept that the criterion is the real question. My criterion is that the prize should honour a discovery that changed what was known, and not a refinement of a platform whose concept already existed. Ciulli's work is excellent and generalised the approach, but it builds on the Crews-Deshaies concept. Cereblon explains how a long-used drug works and opens the glue half, which is a separate and surprising result. I do not think cereblon is only a result about one drug class, since it defines a degron-recruiting mechanism that has since been exploited by design. I would still accept Ciulli as a substitute if the committee decides the citation should be anchored in design rather than mechanism, and I do not want to harden into a position that blocks a five-vote configuration.

responses.point: Linke asks whether I regard the Vancouver trio of Cullis, Hope and Madden as a complete attribution for B041, and whether the 2023 Medicine overlap is disqualifying.
responses.response: I do not regard the trio as complete. The remote-loading and ionizable-lipid work of Cullis, Hope and Madden is the physical-chemical core, but the route to siRNA and mRNA products also runs through MacLachlan and through Anderson and Langer's lipid libraries, and that cannot be assigned cleanly in three names. The 2023 Medicine overlap is not disqualifying in principle, since the delivery vehicle is a separate chemical achievement, but together with the attribution problem it makes B041 a poor choice this year. That is why I moved to B023 and keep B041 only as a second alternative. I accept that Aili, Brzezinski and Chabes ranked it lower for the same reasons.

responses.point: Somfai holds B002 first as a mature and overdue method with a clean two-person attribution, and concedes that degradation may be well timed in a few years.
responses.response: This is the argument that gives me most pause, and the reason B002 is now my first alternative. Buchwald and Hartwig have a clean story, decades of confirmation and an unambiguous citation. The remaining difference for me is that degradation opens a new mode of action, whereas C-N coupling is a further chapter in a field recognised in 2010. I also doubt that waiting a few years is neutral, since a prize for degradation can rest on mechanism that is already confirmed and on approved cereblon-based drugs. I would not call B002 a worse prize in an absolute sense, and I would find it hard to argue against if the committee judged maturity to be decisive.

responses.point: Zou keeps B002 first because both the discovery and the credit are settled, while admitting that she may underweight the novelty of a new drug modality.
responses.response: I agree that settled credit is a real virtue and that B023 does not have it. Where I differ is on whether a three-name cut for B023 is arbitrary. Crews and Deshaies are the clear conceptual pair, and the third seat is a choice between two well-defined strands, not a diffuse spread. I would ask her whether she would move to B023 under a Handa configuration or a Ciulli configuration, or whether the omissions (Sakamoto, Gray, Ito, Kim) are what keep her on B002. If it is the omissions, that is a principled objection that I respect even though I weigh it differently.

responses.point: Aili supports the Crews, Deshaies and Handa citation naming both PROTACs and the cereblon mechanism of molecular glues, and asks whether the two are really one discovery.
responses.response: We agree on the configuration. On the one-versus-two question, I think the shared induced-proximity logic supports one citation, but only if the wording names both mechanisms explicitly, as Aili's, Brzezinski's and Chabes's citations do. A vague phrase about redirecting the ubiquitin-proteasome system would hide the credit to Handa. I have therefore adopted the more explicit wording in my citation, and I still think a two-part PROTAC plus glue prize would be artificial.

uncertainties: Whether Handa or Ciulli takes the third seat, and whether the committee will accept the omission of Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim.
Whether a single citation can cover PROTACs and cereblon-dependent glues without misleading readers about their separate histories.
How much weight the absence of an approved bifunctional degrader should carry, given that thalidomide-class glue drugs are approved.
Whether B002 should win if the committee prizes settled credit and maturity over a new modality.
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged from round 1. I work at Lund University in physical chemistry, as do Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, and I have research overlap with Daniel Aili and Peter Brzezinski on membranes and self-assembly; none of this is recusal-level. I have no personal or institutional tie to Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Buchwald or Hartwig. My field of lipid self-assembly is close to B041 and B021, which I have noted in case colleagues think it affects my judgment of those entries, and I have moved away from B041 as my preferred prize.
